name: Vox V846 Clyde McCoy wah (1967, Halo inductor)
description: Vox / Thomas Organ 'Clyde McCoy' wah-wah (1967), the circuit later sold as the V846: no input buffer, 9 V battery straight onto the circuit. Input 0.01 µF then 68 kΩ into Q1 (BC109B, 22 kΩ collector, 470 Ω emitter); 1.5 kΩ from Q1's base to the resonant node; 500 mH Halo inductor (with its series DC resistance) in parallel with the 100 kΩ McCoy-spec Q resistor down to the bias node (470 kΩ from Q1's collector, 100 kΩ and a 4 µF non-polarised capacitor to ground); 0.01 µF from the resonant node to Q2's emitter. Q2 (BC109B, 1 kΩ collector, 10 kΩ emitter, 470 kΩ base bias from Q1's collector) follows the 100 kΩ audio-taper rocker-pot wiper through 0.22 µF. Output from Q1's collector through 0.22 µF (top of the pot), unbuffered.

sources.title: Fuzz Central, 'Vox Clyde McCoy Wah': McCoy schematic (0.01 µF before the 68 kΩ input resistor, 22 kΩ, 470 Ω, 1.5 kΩ, 470 kΩ ×2, 100 kΩ bias, 4 µF NP, 500 mH, 100 kΩ across the inductor (other McCoys 33 kΩ), 0.01 µF, 0.22 µF ×2, 100 kΩ A pot, 1 kΩ, 10 kΩ; BC109 or BC173 transistors), Halo 'large hole' and 'small hole' inductors, Ducati 4 µF non-polarised cap, 2N3900A service replacement

TC Gakki, 'Legendary Wah-Wah Pedal VOX Clyde McCoy': teardowns of '67 'picture' #120X (Halo large-hole inductor, ICAR 100 kΩ pot, BC109B ×2, Ducati 0.01 µF ×2, Mullard 0.22 µF ×2, Ducati bipolar 4 µF) and '68 'signature' units

Vox Showroom, 'The Thomas Vox Clyde McCoy Wah-Wah Pedal' and 'Vox V846 Wah-Wah Pedal': same circuit as the V846, 9 V battery, 500 mH Halo inductor, 100 kΩ audio-taper pot (ICAR hybrid taper on Italian units)
Vox Showroom, 'VRM-1 Real McCoy reissue': transistor types found in Clyde pedals (2N3900A, 2N2923, 2N2924, BC109), two Halo core variants
Gearnews, 'The VOX Clyde McCoy Wah': Halo inductors, initially the 'large-hole' 30 Ω, later the 80 Ω 'small-hole' version
R. G. Keen, 'The Technology of Wah Pedals' (geofex.com): circuit operation and part roles; earliest wahs reputedly used 470 kΩ-1 MΩ pots, later 100 kΩ
ElectroSmash, 'Dunlop Cry Baby GCB-95 Circuit Analysis': V847 vs GCB-95 differences (V847 R4 510 Ω, R8 100 kΩ, 69.5 kΩ input impedance)

Philips BC109B SPICE card (IS 7.049f BF 381.7 BR 2.359 VAF 59.59 ISE 59.74f NE 1.522 CJE 11.5p CJC 5.38p), as distributed in the LTspice standard.bjt library (licence not stated; quoted as a factual parameter set)

BC109B.note: Philips BC109B SPICE card (LTspice standard.bjt); IKF/NK, ISC/NC, RC and transit times omitted. Datasheet BC109B hFE 200-450 at 2 mA

controls.label: Wah (pedal position)
controls.note: 100 kΩ audio-taper rocker pot: log end to ground, other end on the output, wiper to Q2 via 0.22 µF. 0 = heel down (lowest resonance), 1 = toe down (highest). The Italian ICAR pots had a hybrid lin/log taper (not published); 0..1 spans the whole track

controls.label: Stereo
controls.note: Host stereo/mono routing flag; the pedal is mono. Stored only

controls.label: On/Off
controls.note: The Arrow SPDT footswitch is the host's unit bypass (the real bypass leaves the 0.01 µF input cap in the dry path). The netlist models the effect-on path. Stored only

parts.label: 9 V battery
parts.note: No supply filtering or polarity protection on the 1967 circuit
McCoy order: cap first, then 68 kΩ (Fuzz Central)
Fuzz Central McCoy schematic. ElectroSmash quotes 510 Ω for the later V847

parts.label: Halo inductor 500 mH
parts.note: 500 mH nominal (Vox Showroom, Fuzz Central); replica Halos measure 510-598 mH (PedalPCB thread). Ferrite-core saturation (the 'Halo' character) is not modelled

parts.label: Halo DC resistance
parts.note: unverified: single source (Gearnews): large-hole Halo ≈ 30 Ω (the '67 picture unit #120X had the large-hole type), later small-hole ≈ 80 Ω. Whipple / Sabbadius Halo replicas measure 28.8 / 30.3 Ω (PedalPCB)

parts.label: Q resistor (McCoy spec)
parts.note: unverified which value a given 1967 unit carried: Fuzz Central reports 100 kΩ on some Clyde McCoys and the standard 33 kΩ on others; its schematic shows 100 kΩ

parts.label: Wah pot (ICAR 100 kΩ)
parts.note: unverified: the ICAR hybrid taper is not published; the engine's A (10 % at mid) taper is used, log end on the ground lug
